primary_claim: In toy models with controllable feature co-occurrence, SAE feature absorption occurs whenever features co-occur (even imperfectly, depending on sparsity-penalty strength), producing 'partial absorption' when co-occurring feature magnitudes vary; tying the SAE encoder and decoder weights together eliminates feature absorption in both non-superposition and superposition toy settings.

effect.metric: SAE recovery of true toy feature representations (encoder/decoder cosine similarity to ground truth) before vs. after tying encoder-decoder weights
effect.value: with tied weights the SAE perfectly recovers all true feature representations even under superposition, though MSE loss becomes nonzero (no longer 0 as in the pre-superposition case)

contradicts_or_qualifies: Confirms and mechanistically explains a hypothesis from the authors' previous work ('A is for Absorption') that feature absorption is caused by SAEs struggling to separate co-occurring features, which had been hypothesized but not previously proven
stated_future_work: Test the tied-weights solution on a non-toy SAE
Explore loss terms that encourage encoder/decoder similarity while allowing slight asymmetries, or fine-tune the encoder separately in a second run, to mitigate the higher MSE loss from tied weights
Test the tied encoder/decoder setup on the combo-feature toy model setup, since tying weights may not fix combo-latent issues
Try deconstructing SAEs into denser components using Meta SAEs built from meta-latents
Explore adding an orthogonality loss or other novel loss terms/architectures to solve absorption
limitations_stated: The tied-encoder-decoder fix has not yet been tested on a non-toy SAE
Tying together the encoder and decoder likely results in higher MSE loss
The tied encoder/decoder setup has not been tried on the combo-feature toy model setup, so it may not fix combo-latent issues
quote: Tying the SAE encoder and decoder weights together solves feature absorption in toy models.
